hypotheses.persona: Full-time remote worker with structured morning health routine and consistent home dining habits.
hypotheses.rationale: The 06:45 pill routine persisted on Day 7 (Monday), confirming the health habit is daily, not just weekday. The reading glasses at the counter (06:46) rather than the desk suggests the workday hasn't started yet or the morning routine precedes desk work. The 21:45 plate at cupboard confirms evening meal at home. The pattern of glasses location (Desk on workdays, Counter/Living Room on weekends) remains the strongest discriminator for work vs. leisure, and Day 7's counter location is ambiguous but consistent with a pre-work morning or a very flexible start, leaning towards the 'structured but remote' profile.

hypotheses.persona: Commuter who works from home Mon-Thu but leaves early Friday.
hypotheses.rationale: The persistence of the 06:45 pill routine on Saturday (Day 5) and Sunday (Day 6) strongly contradicts a standard commuter who might have different weekend health habits or sleep in. The Monday counter location for glasses doesn't strongly support this either, as commuters might leave before 06:46. This hypothesis remains weak.

The sustained, identical timing of the pill organizer across 7 days (Mon-Sun) is inconsistent with transient behavior. No signs of packing/unpacking or varied location usage typical of guests. This hypothesis remains highly improbable.
